ce_bugs.text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — Referer header is attacker-controlled and only its host is checked against embeddable_host, so any site can spoof it to trigger retrieve_topic jobs / SSRF-style fetches against the embeddable host for arbitrary paths

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — import_remote(user, t[:link]) passes attacker/import-file-controlled link straight into Kernel#open via TopicEmbed.import_remote/open(url) before any URL-scheme validation, enabling classic Ruby `|command` open() command injection since only TopicEmbed.import (called after the open) validates the http(s) prefix

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied unconditionally, so the transient 'loading' response (which self-reloads via JS) can be cached for a minute even though the topic may already be available on next request

app/models/topic_embed.rb:105 — TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-create on embed_url (unique-indexed) without rescuing a uniqueness violation, so concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g. poll_feed + topic_retriever racing) can raise an unhandled RecordNotUnique instead of gracefully reusing the existing embed

app/models/topic_embed.rb:39 — import_remote fetches arbitrary embed_url via open-uri with no scheme/host allowlist beyond caller checks, enabling SSRF (e.g. internal network requests, redirect-based bypass)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control relies on comparing request.referer host to embeddable_host, but Referer is a client-supplied header that non-browser clients can freely spoof, making this an unreliable security boundary

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:34 — The "no previous embed" test mocks TopicRetriever.new/retrieve entirely, but the controller code enqueues a job (Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)); the test never verifies the actual embed_url/user_id args passed to the job are correct, only that some later TopicRetriever instance responds to retrieve

mrv_findings.text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-30 — TopicEmbed.import does read-then-write (where(embed_url:).first then create!) with no locking/find_or_create_or upsert, so concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs processing the same URL race and one raises an unrescued RecordInvalid/RecordNotUnique from the unique index, aborting the transaction instead of being handled as "already imported".

lib/topic_retriever.rb:38-46 — perform_retrieve checks TopicEmbed.exists? then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inline inside a regular job and checks exists? again, but this reimplements the same racy read-then-write path as TopicEmbed.import and can also fetch/parse the entire feed synchronously inside a request-triggered job just to resolve one embed_url.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-25 — SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) performs an unbounded, untimed-out synchronous HTTP fetch of an external, admin-controlled URL inside a scheduled Sidekiq job with sidekiq_options retry: false, so a slow/hanging remote server stalls the worker for the life of the request with no retry recovery.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:38-46 — import_remote does open(url).read to fetch arbitrary external content synchronously with no timeout/size bound, called from both the scheduled poll path and the per-request RetrieveTopic job, risking worker/job hangs and unbounded memory use on large or slow responses.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3-10 — topic_id and post_id columns are plain integers with null: false but no foreign key constraint and no index on topic_id/post_id (only embed_url is indexed), so TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: post.topic_id) lookups and topic/post associations rely on unindexed columns and DB-level referential integrity is not enforced, allowing orphaned embeds if a topic/post is destroyed.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:5-6 — validates_presence_of :embed_url plus the DB unique index only guarantees uniqueness/non-blankness of the string, not that it is a well-formed absolute URL; the actual invariant enforced by callers (url =~ /^https?\:\/\// in .import) is checked ad hoc before save rather than as a model validation, so a TopicEmbed could be created directly (e.g. via console or future code path) with a non-http embed_url that passes validation.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError on nil for feeds without a content field (e.g. RSS description-only items), and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the whole poll run is silently dropped with no test covering this path (confidence 75, P2).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — `rss.items.each do |i|` has no per-item begin/rescue, so one malformed item (bad link, nil content) aborts processing of all remaining feed items for that poll cycle (confidence 60, P2).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:39 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote` has no rescue for network failures (404/timeout/SSL) from open-uri; an unhandled exception propagates out of the async RetrieveTopic job with no explicit error handling or logging (confidence 55, P2).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `absolutize_urls` treats protocol-relative URLs (e.g. `//evil.com/x`) as root-relative via `start_with?('/')`, producing a mangled URL (`prefix + "/" + "evil.com/x"`) instead of leaving it absolute or handling it correctly (confidence 65, P3).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34-35 — if both `i.link` and `i.id` are blank/non-http, the resulting url fails the regex check inside `TopicEmbed.import` and the item is silently skipped with no logging, so failed imports are unobservable (confidence 50, P3).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, which was only added in Ruby 2.1 (Dec 2013), but the Gemfile targets Ruby 1.9/2.0 ("perftools only works on 1.9 atm"), so this will raise NoMethodError on every feed poll under the app's actual runtime. confidence:75 severity:P1
none — no findings above threshold

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — confidence 75/P0: `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` was added retroactively to an already-applied migration (only whitespace/name changed otherwise), so re-running or replaying it (redo, fresh restore replaying schema_migrations mismatch, manual rerun) will silently DROP the existing top_topics table and lose all cached topic ranking data instead of being a no-op.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — confidence 50/P2: editing the body of a migration that has already run breaks migration content-integrity assumptions (checksums/expectations other devs or CI have of that file), risking divergent schemas across environments that already ran the original version without force: true.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — confidence 50/P2: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true do |t|` is safe on first run since the table is new, but force: true means any future accidental re-run (redo, migrate:reset replay, or manual dup) will drop and recreate topic_embeds without warning, discarding any data already stored there.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — confidence 50/P2: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` adds a NOT NULL column with a default to the posts table, which on large existing posts tables (pre-Rails 5/older MySQL semantics implied by this codebase) triggers a full table rewrite and locks posts for reads/writes for the duration, with no indication the migration accounts for this (no disable_ddl_transaction!, no batched backfill).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:1-41 — task claims "embed URL handling and validation" but this adds an entirely new RSS/ATOM feed-polling subsystem (SimpleRSS, hourly scheduled job, new site settings) unrelated to URL validation, which is scope drift beyond the stated intent.
app/models/post.rb:63-65 — introduces a new cook_methods enum and raw_html rendering bypass on Post, a cross-cutting rendering-pipeline change not implied by "embed URL handling and validation."

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` adds a skip_validations capability to the shared PostRevisor used by all post edits, not just embeds, which is a broader behavioral change to core posting logic than the stated embed-URL scope.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-143 — removal of the `--category` option and category_id assignment logic from the Disqus import task is unrelated to embed URL handling/validation and silently drops previously supported functionality (posts can no longer be imported into a specific category).

Gemfile:209-211 — adding `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` gems for full feed importing/scraping goes beyond "embed URL handling and validation," pulling in a much larger content-extraction feature.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:38-47 — `import_remote` uses ruby-readability to scrape and re-host arbitrary remote page content, which is a content-import feature, not URL handling/validation as scoped by the task.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the attacker-controlled Referer header unescaped into a `<script>` block, allowing a crafted Referer value (e.g. containing `'});</script><script>...`) to break out of the JS string literal and execute arbitrary script (reflected XSS); confidence 75, severity P1.

app/models/post.rb:133 combined with app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — `raw` is returned as `cooked` for `cook_method: raw_html` posts and then rendered via `raw post.cooked`, so remote content fetched by TopicEmbed.import_remote (filtered only by Readability's tag/attribute allowlist, which permits `href`/`src` with no scheme validation, e.g. `javascript:`) bypasses Discourse's normal HTML sanitization pipeline entirely, enabling stored XSS from any embeddable_host page or polled RSS feed; confidence 60, severity P1.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — `ensure_embeddable` authorizes the request by comparing `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the Referer header is fully client-controlled (trivially spoofed with curl/any non-browser client or a stripped/forged header), so this is not a real access boundary despite acting as the sole auth check for the embed endpoint; confidence 90, severity P2.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` checks whether the postMessage sender's origin is a *substring* of the configured discourseUrl rather than an exact/prefix match, so an origin that differs only by port or trailing path segments (e.g. discourseUrl `https://forum.example.com:1234` vs. attacker origin `https://forum.example.com`) can pass the check and have its resize messages accepted; confidence 60, severity P2.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:31 — `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is set unconditionally for every request that passes the (spoofable) referer check, removing framing protection and increasing clickjacking exposure for the embed page; confidence 75, severity P3.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (via lib/topic_retriever.rb fetch_http) performs a server-side fetch of a user-influenced URL; although TopicRetriever#invalid_host? restricts the host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host before calling import_remote, it does not restrict scheme, port, or IP (only hostname string equality), so DNS rebinding or a non-standard port on the same hostname could still be used for SSRF against internal services, and import_remote itself has no independent validation if ever called from another path; confidence 50, severity P2.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:33-42 — every spec in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb mocks/stubs `perform_retrieve` itself (`topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve).once`), so the new `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` branch that calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline is never actually exercised by any test.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38-43 — `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` fully mocks TopicRetriever, so the "success" spec never verifies the controller passes the correct embed_url/opts or that real TopicRetriever#retrieve integrates correctly with the controller.

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` has no test that actually verifies validations are bypassed (e.g. saving otherwise-invalid content with skip_validations: true); spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb's "Supports updating the post" test only checks cooked content changed, not that validation-skipping behavior works or is needed.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor — no spec file covers this task before or after the diff, so removal of the `--category` option and the switch to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is entirely untested (no existing coverage to regress, but also no new coverage added despite the behavioral change).
